paragraph: Upper Saddle River is a single-family market and nothing else, with 54 detached sales over six months against two condo closings that are too few to read. The median sits at $1,688,750, and the sale-to-list ratio of exactly 1.00 with 48 percent of homes going above asking says competitive but not frenzied. Homes are moving quickly when priced right, with a median of 17.5 days on market and a fastest sale of 5 days. Sale prices run from $825,000 to $5,325,000, so the median is the better guide than the average here. On the monthly series, volume built through spring and peaked at 19 closings in June. The May median dropped to $1,352,500 as volume tripled, which is a mix shift toward smaller homes rather than a price decline, and July came back at $1,950,000 on 9 sales. That is resilience where a seasonal drift down would be normal. If the usual Bergen pattern holds, expect closings to thin out through fall while prices stay roughly where they are.
